notable_absence.finding: Nowhere on this page is any Sync Gateway or Couchbase Server role/permission mentioned in connection with configuring the load balancer or reverse proxy - the whole topic is infrastructure-layer (NGINX config, AWS ELB settings, TLS certs) and sits entirely outside both of Sync Gateway's two access-control layers (its own channel/role sync-function model and the server RBAC reused for Admin/Metrics API access).

cross_component_finding: The page's own title is 'Load Balancer' but its first substantive section is 'When to Use a Reverse Proxy', and the NGINX walkthrough configures a single artifact (an nginx server block) that performs BOTH roles at once - proxying/hiding/TLS-termination AND distributing load across multiple upstream Sync Gateway instances. The page never itself distinguishes the two roles terminologically; this extraction separates sgw:reverse-proxy from sgw:load-balancer only because the two capability lists given in the introduction (five reverse-proxy bullets, one of which is load-distribution) read as logically distinct even though NGINX performs both here.
cross_product_finding: The page cites Couchbase Lite's own replicator configuration (six per-platform links: Android/C/C#/Java/Objective-C/Swift) as the client-side lever for the heartbeat interval that the load balancer's keep-alive timeout must be tuned against - a genuine three-product interaction (Couchbase Lite client setting <-> Sync Gateway server default <-> load balancer infrastructure setting) stated entirely through cross-references rather than restated in one place.
